question.stem: An organ pipe of length 0.84 m has one closed end; its other end is open. Sound travels through the air inside it at 340 $\text{m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Show that the wavelength of the first harmonic is about 3.4 m.
markscheme: a quarter of a wavelength fits the pipe (node at the closed end, antinode at the open end), so $\lambda = 4L = 4 \times 0.84 = 3.36\ \text{m}$ ✓

parts.label: b
parts.question: Calculate the frequency of the first harmonic.
markscheme: Accept 98.1 to 105 Hz (using the rounded 3.4 m from (a) gives 100 Hz).

mistakes.feedback: That is the first harmonic of a pipe open at both ends (λ = 2L). For a pipe closed at one end, λ = 4L.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Determine the frequencies of the next two standing waves that can form in this pipe, and state the harmonic number of each.
markscheme: these are the third and fifth harmonics (harmonic number = frequency ÷ first-harmonic frequency) ✓

parts.label: d
parts.question: Explain why a standing wave of twice the frequency of the first harmonic cannot form in this pipe.
markscheme: there must always be a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end ✓
so the pipe length must be an odd number of quarter-wavelengths; twice the frequency would need L = λ/2 (two quarter-wavelengths), which would put a node at the open end ✓

parts.label: e
parts.question: The closed end is opened, so that the pipe is open at both ends. Calculate the new frequency of the first harmonic.
markscheme: antinodes at both ends, so $\lambda = 2L$ and $f = \dfrac{340}{2 \times 0.84} = 202\ \text{Hz}$ ✓

v.what: speed of sound in the air in the pipe

parts.label: a
parts.examinerNote: The first harmonic has a displacement node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end: L = λ/4.

parts.label: b
parts.examinerNote: The wave equation with the wavelength from (a). Either the unrounded wavelength or the value given in (a) may be used: both answers are accepted.

parts.label: c
parts.examinerNote: Two values, so no typed answer. The harmonic number is set by the λ–L relationship, so the second standing wave in a closed pipe is the THIRD harmonic (2028 guidance).

parts.label: d
parts.examinerNote: Only odd harmonics fit the boundary conditions of a pipe closed at one end.

parts.label: e
parts.examinerNote: Open at both ends: half a wavelength fits, so the first-harmonic frequency doubles.
